messages:
sophia: quick note — hit a weird auth behavior when running two AsyncClient instances in one process while using our env-file rotation. client created with explicit api_key gets overridden after rotation.

dan: can you paste a tiny repro?

sophia: sure, gist: create client_a = AsyncClient() (env watcher) and client_b = AsyncClient(api_key=\"sk-b\") then asyncio.gather both generates while flipping the env file between starts. both requests end up with the rotated env key.

kevin: that sounds like the provider is shared globally and mutated on watcher events. is this v0.12.3?

sophia: yep v0.12.3, reproduced locally and in CI.

alex: workaround: pass a concrete AuthProvider per client or always pass api_key. but we should fix the SDK ergonomics.

dan: proposed fix: make clients instantiate an instance-scoped provider when no explicit provider passed and avoid mutating module-level provider after boot. add AuthProvider.from_env_watcher(shared=False) opt-in.

sophia: I'll open an issue + test. test should mock the watcher callback (no real file toggles) and assert Authorization headers per-client.

ci-bot: Created issue #4151: "env-watcher rotation can overwrite explicit per-client api_key due to shared auth provider". Label: devex/bug. Assigned to @sophia.

kevin: also add typing for the provider param in Client.__init__ and update types/redwood.pyi so mypy users see the right signature.

alex: doc ask: add a short section on credential precedence and multi-client examples in the README and examples/multi_client_rotation.py.

sophia: PR draft #4152 posted with failing test and fix. leaving reproduction in PR. marking thread blocked on review. thanks all :partyparrot:
